approaches.name: 1. Cost in Envelopes (the Unit Swap)
approaches.one_liner: Restate a price or fortune nobody can picture as a count of one familiar, cheap unit (lattes, RTX cards, Red Bulls, rice grains, $10K envelopes) and let the count be the punchline.
approaches.why_it_goes_viral: PSYCHOLOGICAL: Magnitude neglect: people can't feel 10^6 vs 10^9, but they can picture a pile of lattes. The unit choice is itself the hook. Youth-coded or topical units (RTX 5090 during the 2026 GPU price spike, iPhone 17 Pro in launch week) trigger an instant 'wait, HOW many?' and a reason to send it. A running counter synced to physical drops works as a progress bar and as ASMR. ALGORITHMIC: No language and probably no VO (the lattes Short returned 'No transcript available'), so it can find seed audiences anywhere. At 11-40 s it gets high completion. Ending on the full pile and cutting back to one unit makes a clean loop, and replays count as views (YouTube since 2025-03-31; Instagram repeat views). The fill-in title template ('Cost in Units of ___') makes every episode a new test. Copycat channels with under 5K subs hit 1.76M-14.9M within weeks.

anatomy: 0.0-1.0 s: title card ('Cost in Units of X' / 'What $N looks like'). A number is on screen in frame 1. No intro, no logo.
1-3 s: first conversion or drop lands with a thud or counter tick. Counter badge fixed at the top (FVIDEOS: white rounded badge, 50.000 € → 100.000 €).
3-20 s: 5-10 escalating items or drops. FVIDEOS runs about 8 drops per 10 s, and each drop works like a cut. Music only, on the beat.
20-24 s: extreme final item or round milestone (1.000.000 €) on the biggest drop.
24-26 s: hard cut back to a single unit, so the loop reads as 'do it again'.
ENVELOPE BUILD 0-1 s: envelope front reads 'COST IN ENVELOPES: [hot item of the week]'; flap stamp reads '1 envelope = $10,000 (source, date)'.
ENVELOPE BUILD 1-15 s: envelopes thud onto a growing stack, the top badge counts up, 4-8 escalating items.
ENVELOPE BUILD ~15 s: the one handwritten 'so what' line the originals lack ('= X years of median pay', sourced).

ENVELOPE BUILD 18-22 s: scale shot with a physically correct stack height (notes × thickness) next to a person, fridge or building. Last 1-2 s: cut to one envelope (loop) and tease the next unit on the flap. Variants: denomination ladder; '[Person] is N× richer than [fictional character]'.

Cost in Units of [cheap, recognisable, topical item]
What $[big number] looks like in [envelopes / $100 bills / Big Macs]
How tall is $[1 billion] in $10K envelopes?
[Person] is [N]x richer than [fictional rich character]
1 [unit] = $[X]. Here's [a billionaire / the national debt / a stadium].
approaches.best_platforms: YouTube Shorts first, at 11-30 s; all core evidence is YouTube, including copies from sub-5K channels at 1.76M-14.9M. Cross-post the same wordless master to Instagram Reels and TikTok. Time episodes to price news and launch weeks.
approaches.pitfalls: (1) The template is saturating, and YouTube's Jul 2025 'inauthentic content' rule plus its Oct 1 2026 Shorts update name 'template-based bulk changes'. Vary the structure and add our own sourced calculation and 'so what' line. (2) Unit choice decides everything (75,736 vs 30.6M on the same channel). Pick units with a live price story. (3) A raw number with no conversion fails (3.62x). (4) Prop cash invites 'fake' debates (the €500 note is no longer issued). Use animated, physically accurate stacks. (5) HD Guy's on-screen content was never watched (vidIQ tags hint at military hardware), so don't assume its visuals. (6) Date and source every unit price.

approaches.name: 2. The Rate Clock
approaches.one_liner: Divide one incomprehensible sum by a human-scale rate ($1/second, $50K/hour, $4B/day) and land on a time or distance you can feel: '15 laps of the Earth', '32 years of your life', 'you'd have started before Julius Caesar was born'.
approaches.why_it_goes_viral: PSYCHOLOGICAL: It turns money into lived time, so the payoff is about mortality, not dollars. There are two payoffs: an early concrete one (Story Snap's distance at about 6 s) and an emotional twist at the end, so viewers stay and rewatch. It is one division viewers can check in their heads, which is pure Fermi. Famous mega-subjects (billionaires, the debt, the 'trillionaire' headline) bring curiosity and polarisation. A 'this guy must be lying, let me check' arc holds even 65 s of uncut calculator footage (sog_geovanie, 1,005.7x on 1.3K followers). ALGORITHMIC: 14-17 s versions loop. Tilbury's math Shorts carry his highest breakouts (11.91x, vs 4.69x for his skits). Timely searches ('elon becomes trillionaire') supply seed audiences. Story Snap's two-sentence Short is the most-viewed in the big-number cluster.

approaches.best_platforms: YouTube Shorts at 14-49 s, where all core evidence sits. TikTok for a 60-110 s fact-check walkthrough. Instagram Reels is untested (literal per-second Reels did not surface as outliers), so treat it as an experiment.
approaches.pitfalls: (1) Rate and calendar errors get torn apart: sog_geovanie's 'AD = After Death' slip, a published guide's per-day-as-per-second figure (an 86,400x error), and 365 vs 365.25. (2) Abstract or jargon framing fails (Rule of 72 best: 29,860 views). (3) Net worth is not cash (Founder Files' contrarian take got 220.51x), so date and source every net-worth figure. (4) Keep inequality a neutral conversion, not a political statement. (5) Celebrity repeats decay (Behind the Border 535x → 29.8x → 5.2x), so rotate subjects and rates. (6) A slow derivation kills a 14 s loop; keep it to one line.

approaches.name: 3. The Read-It Ladder
approaches.one_liner: A 5-8 s single shot where one small recurring number climbs the calendar as a static text block ('$3 a day · $21 a week · $1,080 a year · $10,800 every 10 years'), capped by an anti-guilt or 'now imagine 10' punchline. The text takes longer to read than the clip runs, so it loops.
approaches.why_it_goes_viral: PSYCHOLOGICAL: Viewers map it onto their own habit ('my $27 is iced coffee + DoorDash'), and small × time = shock is the purest envelope move. The best versions flip the expected lecture. '…not enough to buy a nice car so enjoy your caffeine bro' validates the viewer; 'NOW IMAGINE HAVING 10 OF THEM' sells the dream. Both split the YOLO camp from the invest-it camp in the comments. Rounding, deliberate or accidental ($90×12 = $1,080 vs $3×365 = $1,095; '$27/day = $10K' when it is $9,855), brings in the 'math police'. ALGORITHMIC: Read time ≈ runtime, so completion runs past 100% and replays count. Production cost is close to zero. It is the highest-outlier hook type in the IG/TikTok sweep (daily-habit cluster median 285.7x), with the highest small-account multiples in the corpus (1,131x and 1,106x).

approaches.best_platforms: Instagram Reels and TikTok as native 5-8 s loops (music only or silent). YouTube Shorts is proven too (Kel King: 5.19M at 1,131x in 7 s). Export one clean master per platform with no foreign watermarks. A 20-35 s wage-ladder version fits YouTube.
approaches.pitfalls: (1) Lecturing ('skip the latte') is the anti-pattern; the punchline must validate or surprise. (2) Leaving out growth or costs is fine as a labelled hook and toxic as a brand claim. Kel King's '$19,200 made' ignores the purchase price, insurance and depreciation and uses a 48-week year, and 'FIRE YOUR BOSS' brushes YouTube's get-rich-quick policy and the FCA's urgency warnings. (3) It is the easiest format to clone: theme pages copied the '$17.50 after taxes' text word for word within weeks. The handwriting and the front/back flip are the moat. (4) Instagram warns against Reels 'predominantly covered by text', so keep the block short and large. (5) Loops lift reach, not YouTube engaged views, and licensed trending audio cuts the Shorts revenue share.

approaches.name: 4. Two Envelopes (Pick-One Dilemma → Race to the Crossover)
approaches.one_liner: Put two money paths side by side where intuition and math disagree ($1M now vs $1,000/week for life, $200M once vs $20/second, a doubling penny, the early vs the late starter). The viewer picks in second one, then the envelope runs the clock to the break-even or overtake.
approaches.why_it_goes_viral: PSYCHOLOGICAL: The viewer commits silently within 1-2 s, so their ego is invested before any explanation. An ego challenge ('Most people get this WRONG') raises the stakes. The 'obvious' lump sum loses to a rate or exponent, a unit trap: Teacherman's '$1,000 per second' option is $31.5B a year. A tension trough keeps intuition alive (the penny is $163.84 on day 15). Race versions defer WHEN, not WHETHER (Behind the Border's overtake lands at about 55% of runtime) and end on two numbers side by side. ALGORITHMIC: 5-11 s cards loop past 100%. Comment sections become ballots and arguments (day-30 amount vs running total, return rate, horizon). A twist re-hook ('What if it's a dollar per push-up?') restarts the debate. It is the most consistent small-account breakout across YouTube, Instagram and TikTok, and music-only race tickers need no language and are cheap to batch.

approaches.best_platforms: All three. Instagram Reels has the densest small-account breakouts for 'keep 1' polls (305.3x, 224.2x). YouTube Shorts for 5-25 s cards and 45-62 s races (biggest views and multiples: 69.8M, 9.06M, 735.3x, 388.12x). TikTok for a 60-75 s extended solve with a day-by-day counter, which also clears the Creator Rewards length bar.
approaches.pitfalls: (1) Write fresh dilemmas (pension lump sum vs monthly, salary vs signing bonus); the penny is worn out. (2) Always deliver the number, even in a part 2; unresolved rage-bait builds no trust. (3) Arithmetic slips get caught (Zenwish's 'over a million left' is about $0.87M). (4) Define day vs cumulative ($5.37M vs $10.74M). (5) Lump-vs-stream answers depend on the assumed return and horizon, so show both. (6) No screenshots or names of real lottery winners. (7) Unsourced or smoothed celebrity net-worth series (the MBS figures) and projections shown as fact contradict the brand. (8) A named stock as a lane reads as a pick, so use index-style assumptions. (9) Planktin-style 'Like = Cybertruck' interludes are bait that Meta demotes.

approaches.name: 5. The Envelope Split
approaches.one_liner: Take one specific paycheck and split it on screen into labelled envelopes by fixed ratios (55/5/10/15/15 or 50/15/5/30), with the formula morphing into dollars as cash drops. Then add the layer nobody adds: how long each envelope takes to fill and what it becomes.
approaches.why_it_goes_viral: PSYCHOLOGICAL: It is participatory math: every viewer runs the ratios on their own pay. A system that is visible but not yet explained in frame 1 creates curiosity (@moneyletter's 50/15/5/30 cups are on screen before a word is spoken). A numbered open loop shows how much is left. The arc moves from restriction to permission ('do not spend a single dollar' … '$600 guilt-free'). Oddly specific amounts ($5,416.33) read as real and invite comparison, and cash drops are satisfying ASMR. ALGORITHMIC: Frameworks earn saves ('Save for later'). Comment-keyword DM funnels ('Comment BUDGET', 316x) and personalised-reply CTAs ('comment your take-home', 125.1x) drive comments, and 'impossible in my city' starts debates. The paycheck cluster's median outlier is 453.7x. 16 near-identical 'financially free in 5 steps' posts from 13 creators (about 12.7M plays in 90 days) show that demand outlasts saturation. Cash ASMR is the largest raw-reach IG cluster (16.3M across 4 posts).

approaches.name: 6. Same Pile, Different Place (Fixed-Input Countdown)
approaches.one_liner: Hold one number fixed (a $1M salary, a $1M target, one iPhone, one hour of work) and change one thing per beat (country, company, job, year), ordered so the most extreme case lands last.
approaches.why_it_goes_viral: PSYCHOLOGICAL: Only one variable moves, so each beat compares at a glance with no explanation. Viewers place themselves in the list ('where's my country?'). Descending order makes them wait for the extreme (Dubai 'NO TAX', the whole stack pocketed). A scripted interruption ('Excuse me, what about Singapore?') puts the comment section on screen and breaks list fatigue at about 60%. Omissions and rounded figures trigger 'that's not my rate' and 'do my country' comments. ALGORITHMIC: Numbers and flags need no language, so it reaches global seed audiences (1,542 views per subscriber). Expats share it and comment on identity. It produced the largest breakout in the whole corpus: 17,564.8x on a 14.8K-sub channel.

approaches.name: 7. The Sealed-Envelope Estimate (Guess → Build → Open)
approaches.one_liner: Ask a money question people already wonder about (what Jordan Howlett makes, what Monica's apartment would rent for, what a bowling alley clears), make the viewer lock in a guess, build the estimate on the envelope from 3-4 visible inputs in LOW and HIGH columns, then open the sealed envelope for the reported figure.
approaches.why_it_goes_viral: PSYCHOLOGICAL: A famous subject brings built-in curiosity (money voyeurism, 'pocket watching', 'how could Monica afford that?'). Commit-then-reveal (LIE HARD's four panel guesses, 3,339.5x) turns every input into an 'am I close?' check. Each multiplication is a micro-reveal, with the hero number held to about 90% of runtime. Contestable assumptions (an '$8 RPM') drive 'you're wrong' comments, and 'who should I do next?' turns the comment section into the content calendar. ALGORITHMIC: Famous-name keywords tell the platforms which seed audience to test, and named series ('Episode 77') build follows. The Fermi-estimate cluster had the highest median outlier of any IG/TikTok pattern (533.5x). 'How much would it cost to…' breaks out from small fandom and real-estate channels (390x on 4.5K subs), and no finance brand owns the method.

approaches.name: 8. The Trap Card (Envelope Puzzle)
approaches.one_liner: A silent 5-7 s still of a short money puzzle handwritten on an envelope. It names and rules out the tempting wrong answer up front ('It's NOT back to even!') and gives no solution. The comment section is the payoff, and the answer arrives as a flip-the-envelope follow-up.
approaches.why_it_goes_viral: PSYCHOLOGICAL: Instant dissonance: the brain computes the intuitive answer, and the card has already declared it wrong. An ambiguity where both readings feel right splits viewers into camps who correct each other. A permission frame ('Answer without Googling…') turns watching into a test. Viewers who got caught and viewers who feel smart both comment. Handwriting reads as native user content, not an ad. ALGORITHMIC: A still that takes longer to solve than to watch forces pauses and rewatches, pushing retention past 100%, and Instagram counts repeat views. Comment velocity is extreme and production cost is near zero, which allows high cadence. The riddle and money-puzzle IG/TikTok cluster median is 174.4x, and @mathsgenius222 got about 660 views per follower, the most cost-efficient format in the scan.

approaches.name: 9. The Itemized Tally (Receipts & Cost Teardowns)
approaches.one_liner: Walk a familiar price or a real artifact line by line (a 2005 Walmart receipt, the ingredients of a $5.29 Big Mac, the cost stack of a $7 latte, a lottery payout ladder), keeping a running total on a two-column envelope and holding the hero number (total, margin or house edge) to the last seconds.
approaches.why_it_goes_viral: PSYCHOLOGICAL: Each line is a 'higher or lower?' micro-game, and the held total is an open loop. A found artifact supplies proof and curiosity in one sentence ('I found a receipt that's over 20 years old'). A famous price plus a yes/no question ('Is it a rip-off or not?') forces a stance. A planned pattern break at 35-40% resets attention (milk got cheaper; 'but there are hidden costs'). Two numbers side by side ($32.59 vs $73.66) are more shareable than one. Leaving the final subtraction to the viewer drove 5,127 comments on the Big Mac. ALGORITHMIC: Serial micro-payoffs hold completion even at 95 s (Monarch 603x on 4.9K subs). Brand-name search brings reach beyond finance, and the title templates repeat ('Then vs Now:', 'Cost vs Price:').

(2) Substitutions and mixed baskets attract fairness attacks: greeting cards and a DVD made up about 57% of Monarch's increase, so split food from non-food. (3) Without a running total on screen, viewers who can't keep the tally drop off. (4) A long runtime only works with a new number every 3-5 s. (5) Implying that a brand cheats is a legal risk. (6) Gambling topics hit ad-suitability limits, so keep an explicit anti-gambling, expected-value framing, and correct dramatic-but-wrong claims (Matka's '99% the bookie wins') instead of repeating them. Inflation comparisons need sourced CPI.

approaches.name: 10. The Envelope Audit (Claim Check)
approaches.one_liner: Paraphrase a viral money claim in second one ('I write off my private chef', '$400/week from a $3K car', 'just pay the minimum'), credit its true part, then red-pen the missing lines on the envelope until the honest number and a verdict stamp appear.
approaches.why_it_goes_viral: PSYCHOLOGICAL: A debunk is a built-in open loop: 'is this real?' is only answered at the verdict. An outrageous claim with visible disbelief in the first 1.5 s validates the viewer's own skepticism. There is a double payoff: either the claim survives correction (the fixed trillion calculation is still under $1T) or it collapses ('a write-off is a coupon worth your tax rate, not a free meal'). Believers and skeptics both comment, and viewers send it to 'the friend who writes everything off'. ALGORITHMIC: It drives comment velocity and reaches beyond finance (small-business owners, tax TikTok, side-hustlers). The supply of claims is effectively endless: about 70% of graded high-view finance TikToks scored C or lower. Meta doesn't recommend low-quality finance content, so correct, sourced math stays recommendable. Vivian Tu credits her 3M-view, 100K-follower first week to 'I actually showed people the math.' Tiny professional accounts hit 220-1,507x with this framing.

anatomy: Money Guy (36 s), 0-22 s: split screen; the claim escalates in word-by-word captions ('EVERY SINGLE YEAR / MONTH / DAY') while the hosts cringe.

22-36 s: host role-play, then the punchline ('I'm not your father tonight, I'm the CEO') over a red-X stock photo, and a hard end. Zero numbers. sog_geovanie variant: claim 0-34 s, 'this gotta be lying', a 65 s uncut calculator segment, payoff in the last 8 s.
ENVELOPE BUILD 0-2 s: the claim as a quote card in our own graphics ('Finance TikTok says: write off your private chef') with a red AUDIT stamp. No stitch.
ENVELOPE BUILD 2-4 s: 'Let's audit it on one envelope.' The claim's headline number is written large.
ENVELOPE BUILD 4-8 s: credit the claim's true part first (e.g. $3,000 ÷ $400 = 7.5-week payback); fairness keeps believers watching.

ENVELOPE BUILD 8-22 s: 3-5 red-pen strike-throughs, each with −$X and a scratch SFX (skipped costs, tax rate, the 50% business-meal limit, 52 vs 48 weeks, expected value); illustrative inputs marked 'assume'.
ENVELOPE BUILD 22-28 s: verdict stamp, the circled honest number and a one-line rule ('A write-off is a coupon worth your tax rate, not a free meal': a $100 dinner ≈ $76 at an assumed 24% bracket).

ENVELOPE BUILD 28-35 s: a question that splits the comments ('Still want the chef at $76 a night?'), then cut to the claim card (loop). Quantify what talking heads skip: $5,000 at 22% APR paying interest + 1% ≈ 230 months (~19 years), ≈ $13,100 paid (illustrative).
hook_formulas: Finance TikTok says "[claim]". Let's audit it on one envelope.
"[Outrageous claim]." Sounds fake. Here's the envelope math.
They said $[X]. They forgot [the one cost that matters].
Is $[X] really enough to [goal]?
Why you're wrong about [famous number]
Written off ≠ paid off.
approaches.best_platforms: YouTube Shorts at 30-40 s (Money Guy, Founder Files, Straight Arrow) and TikTok at 60-110 s audit cuts (sog_geovanie, @financeunfiltered2). An Instagram quote-card version built for sends to 'the friend who believes this'.
approaches.pitfalls: (1) Don't stitch, re-upload or screen-record other creators' clips (sog_geovanie's source was a repost; Money Guy's format is a reaction). These are the riskiest originality moves under YouTube's Oct 1 2026 and Instagram's Apr 30 2026 rules, so paraphrase on a card instead. (2) Never name, mock or accuse a private creator of fraud; audit claims, not people. (3) Tax, debt and investing verdicts must stay illustrative (FCA, ESMA, SEC exposure): cite the rule and say 'terms vary'. (4) An audit with a wrong number is fatal to this brand. (5) Smugness kills warmth, so credit the true part first. (6) It needs a steady weekly claim scan, and absolute views for small-channel audits are modest (304K, 319K); the 6.2M Money Guy example is a reaction format we can't copy.

cross_cutting_principles: THE CONVERSION IS THE HOOK, NOT THE NUMBER. Raw mega-numbers underperform: 'How much is a billion dollars?' got 3.62x on a 1.52M-sub channel, 'The national debt is hard to comprehend' 1.35x, and news-style '$38T debt' Shorts 3-11x. The same numbers turned into units, time or a dilemma break out: Story Snap 9.4M at 150.55x, InFocus 14.9M on 3.49K subs, Filomation 5.66M at 388x.

RIDE A FAMOUS NOUN; NEVER TITLE WITH JARGON. 'Latte factor' returned 0 finance Shorts, but 'Cost in Units of Starbucks Lattes' got 9.86M. The best strict 'Rule of 72' Short got 29,860 views. Schwab's compound-interest explainer got 23K and Acorns' 15.5K. WhiteBoard Finance's best Short got 19.7K despite 1M+ long-form subs. Nearly every 10M+ math Short rides on McDonald's, Starbucks, RTX, iPhone, Elon, Friends or Walmart.

FRAME 1 = TITLE = ON-SCREEN TEXT = FIRST SPOKEN LINE, AND IT CONTAINS A NUMBER OR A DILEMMA. All five transcribed puzzle and business outliers open on their title question. Monica's question is triple-redundant, and Joey Viola's first words are step one. TikTok's ad data: over 63% of top-CTR videos land the key message within 3 s. YouTube's 'stayed vs swiped away' and Instagram's 3-second Skip rate measure exactly this.

TWO LENGTH MODES; DEAD SENTENCES KILL, NOT LENGTH. Mode A is the 4-8 s read-it loop (mightym 7.6 s 1,106x; Kel King 7 s 1,131x; mathsgenius 5 s 522x; Filomation 6 s 388x). Mode B is the 45-155 s walkthrough where every sentence adds a number (Monarch 95 s 603x; Regalis 88 s 244x; jamaal 152 s 908x; se33y 106 s 591x). Of the top six big-number Shorts, three are 14 s or shorter and three run 61-95 s. Cut each master per platform: about 25 s YouTube, 45-60 s Instagram, 61-75 s TikTok.

PAY OFF EARLY, HOLD THE HERO NUMBER, BREAK THE PATTERN AT 35-40%. Story Snap pays off distance at about 6 s and the twist at 14 s. Monica's $8,000 lands at 54/60 s, jamaal's $1.06M at 140/152 s, Monarch's total in the final line. Monarch's milk got cheaper at about 0:33 and Behind the Border overtakes at about 55%. Two final numbers side by side spread better than one ($32.59 vs $73.66; ₹5 Cr vs ₹11.5 Cr).

MAKE THE VIEWER COMMIT BEFORE THE REVEAL. Dilemmas (Teacherman 735x, Alaric 422x, Filomation 388x), guess-the-price (LIE HARD 3,339x; bris 212x; Jolene Erdman 174x) and puzzle cards (mathsgenius 522x) are the most consistent tiny-channel breakouts. A silent pick in 1-2 s invests the ego, and viewers comment to defend it.

NOBODY SHOWS THE MATH, AND THAT IS BOTH THE WHITESPACE AND THE TRUST MOAT. Dr Bandana never computes the $41.7M/hour. Granny Drive never computes the 116-day break-even. Monarch never adjusts for CPI. Tilbury never states the margin. CoComelon's '$11M/mo' is never derived. Money Guy and Sklar show zero numbers. Published money math is often wrong (an 86,400x per-second error; about 70% of graded finance TikToks at C or lower). A visible 1-3 line envelope calculation with labelled assumptions and a range is a differentiator no outlier owns.

USE CORRECTABLE ROUNDING AND OPEN LOOPS AS THE COMMENT ENGINE, DELIBERATELY AND LABELLED. Examples: @anatalksmoney's '$27/day = $10K' ('math police', 491x), Fairy Tanton's correctable 30% tax estimate (1.29M), Tilbury's unstated margin (5,127 comments), Teacherman's withheld answer (735x). The brand-safe version is an openly labelled '≈' figure, the exact number pinned, and a genuine question. Meta demotes 'comment YES' bait.

TINY ACCOUNTS BREAK OUT; THE FORMAT DOES THE WORK. IG/TikTok accounts under 5K followers had a 174.4x median outlier, against 18.6x for 500K+. YouTube breakouts came from channels with 841 to 14.8K subs (AJ 17,565x; FVIDEOS 890x; Monarch 603x; Cost of War 1.76M on 841 subs). Big channels posting big numbers sit at 1-4x (Graham Stephan 3.75x, Fahad Riaz 3.62x). Every platform tests each post on a seed audience regardless of followers.

SERIES TEMPLATES COMPOUND, BUT SAME-SUBJECT REPEATS DECAY, SO ROTATE THE VARIABLE. Named series earn follows: HD Guy's 9 'Cost in Units' episodes, 'Pocket Watching' Ep. 77, Bran's $/hour houses, Tilbury's 'Cost vs Price', 'Day 2 of Excellent Indian Businesses'. Repeats decay fast (Behind the Border 535x → 29.8x → 5.2x; Planktin 153x → 5.52x), and HD Guy's episodes range from 75,736 to 30.6M depending on the unit.

RIDE THE PRICE STORY OF THE WEEK. RTX 5090 got 30.6M and DDR5 2.59M during the 2026 price spike. iPhone 17 Pro got 14.9M in launch week on 3.49K subs. sog_geovanie rode the live 'elon becomes trillionaire' search. Matka newsjacked the 'Matka King' series, and 8th Pay Commission salary cards hit 853.2x.

FACELESS WORKS WHEN THE NUMBER EARNS THE ATTENTION A FACE WOULD. Faceless outliers: Cost in Units (likely no VO), FVIDEOS (hands, 890x), mightym (hand and can, 1,106x), mathsgenius (still paper, 522x), @hoooon492 (stick figures, 713x), @investment_timeline (animated chart, 141x), Story Snap (VO over walking, 150.55x), Planktin (animation, 153x). Charisma-led winners (jamaal's 60 s biography, se33y's car vlog, AJ's street skit) must be rebuilt with the number first and a running total on screen.

DESIGN FOR SENDS, SAVES AND COMPLETION. Instagram's top signals are watch time, likes per reach and sends per reach, with sends weighted most for non-followers. Frameworks earn saves (Joey's 'Save for later'). Comment-keyword lead magnets work on Instagram ('Comment BUDGET' 316x; 'comment your take-home' 125.1x). A direct caption question earned Humphrey 4-6× more comments per view. Build a taggable person into every script.

SPECIFIC NUMBERS READ AS TRUE; ROUND NUMBERS READ AS GOALS. Odd specifics recur among top performers ('$5,416.33' 3.2M, '$713.59', '$17.50 after taxes', '$27.40 a day', '$5.29 Big Mac', '17 items cost $32.59'). Use specific numbers for inputs and artifacts, and round power-of-ten figures ($1M, $1B, $1T) as milestones.

ORIGINAL ASSETS ONLY, AND TEACH MATH, NOT PICKS. Our own handwriting and animation; no TV or creator clips (Seinfeld 246x, Futurama 1,442x and Friends-clip outliers are copyright traps; a YouTube Short over 1 minute with a Content ID claim is blocked). State assumptions on screen ('7%/yr assumed, before fees and taxes'). No get-rich-quick titles, no named-ticker calls, no personalised advice. Discount paid outliers (like rate under ~0.3%) when benchmarking.
platform_rules: All three platforms test every post on a small seed audience regardless of follower count: TikTok says follower count and past hits are not direct For You factors (https://techcrunch.com/2020/06/18/tiktok-explains-how-the-recommendation-system-behind-its-for-you-feed-works); Instagram shows posts 'to a small audience' first (https://techcrunch.com/2024/04/30/instagram-is-updating-its-ranking-systems-to-surface-more-content-from-smaller-original-creators); YouTube Shorts finds a 'seed audience' per Short (https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/388588/). A zero-subscriber channel can break out on its first good post. [OFFICIAL]

The first decision is stay-or-swipe, and the platforms report it directly: YouTube's 'Viewed vs. swiped away / Stayed to watch' (https://www.searchenginejournal.com/youtube-explains-how-shorts-algorithm-works/494953/) and Instagram's 3-second Skip rate, added Aug 2025 (https://metricool.com/instagram-reel-analytics/). TikTok ad data: over 63% of top-CTR videos show the key message in the first 3 s (https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en-US/blog/9-creative-tips-to-drive-auction-ad-performance).

Instagram's top three signals are watch time, likes per reach and sends per reach; sends matter most for non-followers (https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/instagram-shares-algorithm-insights-2025/738034/). Every Reel needs a 'send this to…' person. [OFFICIAL]

TikTok's strongest stated signal is whether a user finishes a longer video (https://newsroom.tiktok.com/en-us/how-tiktok-recommends-videos-for-you/). Videos over 60 s get 43.2% more reach (Buffer, 1.1M videos: https://buffer.com/resources/longer-tiktoks-get-more-views-data/), and only videos over 1 minute earn Creator Rewards (https://metricool.com/tiktok-creator-next/).

Length sweet spots differ by platform: YouTube creators favour under 30 s (Adobe, 507 creators: https://www.adobe.com/express/learn/blog/youtube-shorts-length-study); Instagram Reels of 45-60 s had the highest median views (Socialinsider, ~140K Reels: https://socialinsider.io/blog/instagram-reels-length/); TikTok favours over 60 s. Cut one master three ways (~25 s / ~45 s / ~65 s).

View counting changed. Since 2025-03-31 a YouTube Shorts view counts on every start and replay; Engaged views exclude loops and drive earnings (https://www.tubefilter.com/2025/03/26/youtube-shorts-views-counting-stats/; https://says.com/my/tech/youtube-shorts-new-metric). First-frame counting extended to all formats on 2026-08-24 (https://www.tubefilter.com/2026/08/18/youtubes-now-counting-public-views-from-the-first-frame-hoping-inflated-numbers-will-help-creators-negotiate-brand-deals/). Instagram Views include repeat views (https://www.socialpilot.co/instagram-marketing/instagram-views-metrics-changes). Loops buy reach, not YouTube earnings, so judge our work on engaged views and stayed-to-watch.

Originality is enforced in recommendations. YouTube's 'inauthentic content' rule (Jul 15 2025) targets templates with minimal variation (https://www.plagiarismtoday.com/2025/07/08/youtube-targets-inauthentic-content/). YouTube's Oct 1 2026 Shorts update says 'VO descriptions of what's happening on screen, minor technical edits, or template-based bulk changes' are not original (https://www.relevantaudience.com/youtube/youtube-shorts-original-content-reach-update/; https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/10/youtube-cuts-reach-reuploaded-shorts-originality-push.html). Instagram (Apr 30 2026) removes aggregators from recommendations, and 75% of US recommendations now come from original posts (https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/30/instagram-restricts-reach-of-content-aggregators-in-new-crackdown/). TikTok makes unoriginal or watermarked re-uploads For You-ineligible (https://onlineoptimism.com/blog/updates-tiktoks-community-guidelines).

Copyright trap: a YouTube Short over 1 minute with any active Content ID claim is blocked globally (https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877?hl=en). Licensed music reduces the creator's Shorts revenue share (https://vidiq.com/blog/post/youtube-shorts-monetization/). Use original or royalty-free audio and no TV or creator clips.

AI and 'slop' risk: cutting low-quality AI content is a stated 2026 YouTube priority (https://www.eweek.com/de/news/youtube-ai-slop-crackdown-creators/). Kapwing found 21% of the first 500 Shorts shown to a new account were AI-generated (https://the-decoder.com/one-in-five-youtube-shorts-shown-to-new-users-is-ai-generated-slop-study-finds/). TikTok added an AI slider so users can see less AI content (https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-tiktok-ai-content/). Realistic synthetic content needs a disclosure label; animated envelopes do not (https://9to5google.com/2024/03/18/youtube-altered-content-disclosure/). A recognisable human voice and hand-drawn style protect a faceless channel.

Meta demotes engagement bait ('comment YES', 'tag a friend', vote-baiting) (https://www.searchenginejournal.com/facebook-demoting-engagement-bait/228071), and does not recommend 'sensitive or low-quality' finance content (https://www.socialsamosa.com/2020/09/facebook-highlights-recommendation-guidelines). Ask genuine questions and keep the math accurate.

Instagram warns against Reels 'predominantly covered by text' and makes other-app watermarks less discoverable; your own logo is fine (https://tubefilter.com/2021/02/10/instagram-reels-with-tiktok-watermark-less-discoverable/; https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/instagram-clarifies-including-your-own-logo-on-a-reel-is-ok/730852/). Hashtags are capped at 5 (https://www.blogdumoderateur.com/instagram-limite-hashtags-5-par-publication/). Trial Reels test on non-followers only (https://routenote.com/blog/how-to-test-reels-with-non-followers-on-instagram/).

Cadence and reposting: YouTube's Shorts lead says posting more does not by itself widen reach, and deleting and re-uploading is treated as spam (https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/youtube-shares-advice-for-shorts-creators-including-notes-on-hashtags-the/691835/). Buffer data points to 3-5 posts a week on Instagram (https://buffer.com/resources/how-often-to-post-on-instagram/), and TikTok views per post keep rising up to 11+ a week (https://buffer.com/resources/how-often-should-you-post-on-tiktok/).

Captions and sound: 69% of US adults watch sound-off in public, and 80% are more likely to finish with captions (https://www.streamingmedia.com/Articles/News/Online-Video-News/80-of-Video-Caption-Users-Arent-Hearing-Impaired-Finds-Verizon-131860.aspx). 88% of TikTok users say sound is essential (https://roirevolution.com/blog/july-2021-social-media-water-cooler/). Burn in captions and also use voice or SFX.

Monetization: the YouTube Partner Program bar today is 1,000 subs plus 10M Shorts views in 90 days. From Feb 1 2027, new applicants need 1,000 subs plus 20M qualified Shorts views in 90 days or 8,000 watch hours, and everyone needs a rolling 10M per 90 days to keep Shorts pool revenue (https://blog.youtube/news-and-events/youtube-partner-program-updates-2027-new-opportunities-earn/). Shorts RPM is about $0.03-$0.10 per 1K (https://vidiq.com/blog/post/youtube-shorts-monetization/). Shorts are for discovery; long-form, products and sponsors pay.

Finance-specific rules: TikTok bans branded content for all financial products (https://www.savings.com.au/savings-accounts/the-end-of-fintok-tiktok-bans-crypto-and-finance-related-branded-content). YouTube bans 'get rich quick' promises and misleading titles (https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2801973). FTC: disclosures go in the video, spoken if the endorsement is spoken (https://www.dwt.com/insights/2023/07/ftc-advertising-endorsement-and-testimonial-guides). UK FCA FG24/1: unauthorised promotion of regulated products can be a criminal offence (https://fca.org.uk/publications/finalised-guidance/fg24-1-finalised-guidance-financial-promotions-social-media). ESMA (Jan 2026): a 'not investment advice' disclaimer does not protect you (https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/press-release-of-12-january-2026-finfluencers-). Teach math, not picks, with assumptions stated on screen.
whitespace: The proven viral formats (unit swaps, rate clocks, dilemmas, read-it ladders, receipt tallies, pop-culture estimates) almost never show their arithmetic, and when they do it is often wrong. Examples: AJ's single unexplained tax rates; the Kel King video's 48-week 'year' with no costs; sog_geovanie's 'AD = After Death' error; jamaal's unsourced $8 RPM; Matka's '99% the bookie wins'; a published guide's 86,400x per-second error. About 70% of graded high-view finance TikToks scored C or lower. Back of the Envelope can own one recognisable ritual: a 1-3 line calculation handwritten on an envelope, with labelled assumptions, a LOW-HIGH range where inputs are uncertain, a postmark-style source stamp, and its own rounding made into a deliberate 'math police' joke ('≈', exact figure pinned). Five specific gaps support this. (1) Implicit Fermi estimation ('How much would it cost to…', 'Cost in Units of…') reaches millions (Monica 390x on 4.5K subs; HD Guy 30.6M), but it belongs to fandom, gaming, sports and real-estate channels with no finance brand or recurring method. Humphrey Yang's 'Estimating Sales' proved demand at 6.8M-10.6M and has no 2024-2026 episodes in his top 50. (2) The terms 'napkin math' and 'envelope math' are unowned for money: the only finance 'napkin math' Short had 31,266 views, and no Fermi or market-sizing Short broke out. So lead with the famous subject and make the method the visual signature, not the keyword. (3) Cash-stuffing (#cashstuffing ≈ 1.9B TikTok views; the 100 Envelope Challenge 150M+) has no math layer: nobody covers time-to-fill, the Gauss sum behind the $5,050 challenge, or inflation's drag on cash. On YouTube the category tops out at 146K, and the brand name owns both meanings of 'envelope'. (4) Polished, physically accurate scale visualisation (envelope towers, stack heights, weights) is scarce on Shorts. (5) Accuracy is a positioning edge in a low-trust category: Vivian Tu's breakout was 'I actually showed people the math.' The sweet spot is the overlap of an implicit-estimation title about a famous noun, a story, dilemma or unit wrapper, and the shown, sourced envelope method. Each video carries an original calculation, which also protects reach under the 2025-2026 originality and anti-template rules.
